summary:
The design language is "The Examiner's Folio": a forensic-finance interface art-directed like a private bank's annual report crossed with a broadsheet ledger and a rare-books catalog. Everything sits on warm, unbleached paper tones rather than screen-white; text is near-black ink (never pure #000, which reads as digital, not printed); the single authoritative color is a deep bottle/racing green used for structure, emphasis and interactive states; a restrained brass and an oxblood serve as the only other pigments. The oxblood does double duty as the traditional "red ink" of debits and as the flag color for suspect entries — which is historically correct and instantly legible to a forensic accountant. Nothing glows, nothing is glassmorphic, nothing has a drop shadow deeper than a sheet of paper resting on a desk.

Typography carries the luxury. Fraunces (a soft, slightly wonky old-style display serif on Google Fonts) sets headlines and exhibit titles with real character; Newsreader, drawn for editorial text, handles body copy and annotation with true italics; IBM Plex Mono at 400/500 sets every numeral in ledgers, giving perfectly tabular figures with a bureaucratic, evidence-locker precision. Structure is drawn with hairline rules — 0.5–1px lines in ink at low opacity, double rules above totals, thick-thin "Oxford" rules under section mastheads — exactly as a broadsheet or a bound financial statement would. Cards are replaced by rule-bounded regions on continuous paper; whitespace and rules do the separating, not boxes and shadows.

Charts and motion follow the same discipline: 1–1.5px strokes, no fills or at most a 4–6% green tint, baseline-only axes, no gridline lattice, direct labels instead of legends, annotations set in Newsreader italic like a marginal note from the examining partner. Motion is limited to opacity fades and small vertical settles (120–200ms, ease-out), numbers that tick like a mechanical counter when totals recompute, and a slow underline draw on rules — never spring physics, never bounce, never parallax. The overall effect: the software feels like a meticulously typeset case file that happens to be interactive, which is precisely the register that earns a forensic accountant's trust.
key_points: COLOR — Paper grounds: #F7F3EA (primary page background, warm unbleached paper), #FBF8F1 (raised sheet / table background, one 'ply' lighter), #EFE8D9 (recessed wells, sidebar, aged-paper zones), #E6DECB (hover/selected row tint, like a pencil shading). Never pure white anywhere.

COLOR — Ink: #1C1B16 (primary text, warm near-black iron-gall ink), #57534A (secondary text/captions), #8A8375 (tertiary/disabled, 'faded ink'). Never #000000 and never cool grays (#333/#666 are forbidden — they read as screen, not print).

COLOR — Deep green primary: #1E3A2F (bottle green — links, active states, primary buttons, chart primary series), #142B22 (hover/pressed and dark masthead panels), #2E5943 (lighter green for secondary chart series), #DCE5DD (green wash for subtle highlight fills at ~100% — use instead of alpha overlays on paper).

COLOR — Secondary accents, used sparingly (<5% of any screen): brass/gilt #9C7C46 (rules on mastheads, exhibit numbers, seals, 'gold-tooled' details; lighter tint #C4A96B for fine gilt hairlines) and oxblood #6E2B31 (bookbinding leather; reserved for gravity: flags, adverse findings).

COLOR — Semantic ledger colors derived from the palette, not from SaaS red/green: CREDIT #2F5D45 (restrained green, close to primary so credits feel 'normal', not celebratory), DEBIT #8C3A3D (red-ink tradition — muted madder red, works on paper without vibrating), FLAGGED/SUSPECT #6E2B31 oxblood paired with a #F3E4DE wash and a 2px oxblood left rule on the row; NEUTRAL/UNVERIFIED #9C7C46 brass for 'pending examination'. Success/error toasts reuse CREDIT/DEBIT colors — no new hues.

TYPE — Google Fonts pairing: Display = 'Fraunces' (variable; use weights 350–400 for large headlines, 600 for small-caps labels; opsz axis high for headlines; its slight wonk gives rare-books character). Body = 'Newsreader' (400 body, 500 emphasis, true italics for annotations/marginalia — it was drawn for editorial reading). Numerals/ledger = 'IBM Plex Mono' 400 and 500 (inherently tabular, bureaucratic-precise; use for ALL money figures, account numbers, dates in tables, timestamps). All three confirmed on fonts.google.com.

TYPE — Scale (print-derived, modest ratio ~1.25 with a jump at display sizes): 12px caption/labels (Fraunces 600 letterspaced small caps, tracking +0.08em), 14px table body & UI (Newsreader 400 or Plex Mono for figures), 16px body copy (Newsreader 400, line-height 1.6), 20px section heads (Fraunces 500), 28px page heads (Fraunces 400), 40px display (Fraunces 350–400, line-height 1.1, opsz max), 56px hero/report-cover only. Money figures in tables: 14px Plex Mono; hero KPI figures: 40px Plex Mono 400 (mono at display size = evidence, not marketing).

RULES/BORDERS — Broadsheet grammar: standard hairline #1C1B16 at 15% opacity (or solid #DDD5C4), 1px, never 2px for ordinary division. Section mastheads get an 'Oxford rule' (2px + 0.5px pair, brass or ink). Financial totals follow accounting convention exactly: single rule above a subtotal, DOUBLE rule (two 1px lines, 2px apart) beneath a final total. Column separators in tables: none — alignment does the work; horizontal hairlines between row groups only, not every row. No rounded corners above 2px radius anywhere; 0px on tables and rules.

TABLES/LEDGERS — Right-align every numeric column; decimal-align via tabular mono. Column heads in 12px Fraunces small caps with a hairline beneath. Negative amounts and debits in #8C3A3D, optionally wrapped in accountant's parentheses (1,240.00) — offer this as a display preference, practitioners will notice. Zebra striping forbidden; use generous 12–14px row padding and hairlines every 5 rows (like ruled ledger paper). Row hover = #E6DECB wash, no shadow. Currency symbol set once in the column head, not per cell. Flagged rows: oxblood 2px left rule + wash, and a superscript exhibit mark (†, ‡, or Ex. 12) linking to the finding.

TEXTURE — Paper feel without kitsch: NO skeuomorphic paper JPEG textures, torn edges, or coffee stains. Achieve it with (a) the warm palette itself, (b) an extremely subtle SVG turbulence/noise overlay at 1.5–2% opacity, ~200px tile, luminosity blend, (c) shadows that behave like stacked sheets: 0 1px 0 rgba(28,27,22,.06) plus 0 8px 24px rgba(28,27,22,.05) max — a sheet lying on a desk, never floating, (d) 'deckle' restraint: at most one decorative element per view (a brass seal, a folio number), (e) letterpress is faked by nothing — no inner text shadows.

CHARTS — 1.25–1.5px strokes in bottle green #1E3A2F, second series #2F5D45 or brass #9C7C46, flagged periods in oxblood. Area fills at most a 5% green tint or fine 45° hatching (hatching is very on-language for forensic exhibits). Axes: baseline only, hairline; NO gridline lattice — 2–3 dotted reference lines maximum, labeled inline. No legends: label lines directly at their right terminus in 12px Newsreader italic. Annotations styled as examiner's marginalia: thin brass leader line to an italic note. Bars: 1px ink outline, paper or 8% green fill, square corners. Data points invisible until hover; hover marker = 3px ink dot + hairline crosshair. Tooltips = a small paper card with hairline border, no shadow blur beyond 8px.

MOTION — 'Nothing moves that ink cannot do.' Durations 120–200ms UI, 300–400ms page-level; easing cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1) or ease-out only — springs, bounce, overshoot, parallax, and scale-pops are banned. Permitted vocabulary: opacity fades, 4–8px vertical settle (a sheet laid down), rules that draw themselves left-to-right on section entry (300ms), recomputed totals that tick digit-by-digit like a mechanical counter (400ms, mono keeps width stable), flag application = the oxblood left rule draws downward once (deliberate, like a pen stroke). Skeletons are faint hairline placeholders, never shimmering gradients. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by dropping to instant with fades.

LAYOUT — 12-column grid, max content width ~1200–1280px, generous 32–48px margins; a persistent narrow 'marginalia' column (like a rare-book gloss) for annotations, exhibit references, and audit-trail notes. Page headers styled as report mastheads: matter name in Fraunces, engagement/case number in Plex Mono, date, thick-thin brass rule beneath. Folio conventions in the chrome: page/section numbers, 'Prepared by / Reviewed by' fields — the UI itself mimics working-paper standards (which maps to real audit sign-off workflows).

ICONOGRAPHY — 1px-stroke line icons only, drawn to match the hairline weight, in ink or green; no filled or duotone icons. Where possible replace icons with typographic marks a practitioner knows: †, ‡, §, ¶, 'Ex.', 'cf.', ✓ (tick-mark culture from audit working papers — actual tick marks like ^, T, F for footed/traced/verified is a deep in-joke that lands hard with this audience).
terminology: Tick marks — the standardized symbols (F = footed, T = traced, V = vouched, ^ = agreed) auditors annotate on working papers to show what procedure was performed on a figure.
Footing / cross-footing — verifying a column total (footing) and that row totals agree with column totals (cross-footing).
Vouching vs. tracing — vouching follows a recorded entry back to its source document (tests existence/occurrence); tracing follows a source document forward into the records (tests completeness).
Exhibit — a document formally entered as evidence, numbered ('Exhibit 12' / 'Ex. 12'); forensic reports attach schedules and documents as lettered/numbered exhibits.
Working papers — the auditor/examiner's documented evidence file, with preparer/reviewer sign-offs and cross-references.
Schedule — a supporting table in a report (e.g., 'Schedule of Unexplained Deposits'); the natural name for any ledger-style view in this app.
Double rule — the two parallel lines drawn under a final total in formal accounting presentation; single rule above a subtotal.
Red ink / debit convention — the bookkeeping tradition of writing debits, deficits and overdrawn balances in red; origin of 'in the red'.
Tabular (lining) figures — numerals of uniform width so digits align vertically in columns; mandatory for ledgers, the opposite of proportional oldstyle figures.
Accountant's parentheses — rendering negative amounts as (1,240.00) rather than with a minus sign.
Benford's Law — the expected logarithmic distribution of leading digits in natural financial data; deviation is a classic fraud-screening test.
Chain of custody — the documented, unbroken record of who handled evidence and when; the audit-trail concept forensic accountants expect for every document.
Oxford rule (thick-thin rule) — the paired heavy+light rule used under mastheads in fine bookwork and broadsheets.
Marginalia / gloss — annotations set in the margin of a text, the model for this UI's annotation column.
Folio — a page/leaf number in a bound volume; used here for the app's page and section numbering chrome.
demo_ideas: The Evidence Exhibit viewer: a scanned bank statement or invoice mounted like a rare-books catalog plate — centered on the paper background with a hairline ink frame, a brass 'EXHIBIT 12-B' plate in Fraunces small caps above it, and a chain-of-custody strip in Plex Mono beneath (received date, source, hash, examiner initials). Extracted transactions render alongside in a ledger table, and hovering a table row draws a thin brass leader line to the exact region of the scan it was extracted from.

The Schedule of Findings, typeset like a court schedule: 'Schedule 3 — Unexplained Transfers, In the Matter of Meridian Holdings LLC' with an Oxford rule masthead, columns in tabular Plex Mono, debits in muted red-ink parentheses, a single rule above the subtotal and a true double rule under the grand total that draws itself in over 300ms when the figures finish ticking up — an accountant will physically feel that double rule.

Examiner's tick marks as the interaction model: instead of checkboxes, the analyst stamps real audit tick marks on figures — a small mark palette (F footed, T traced to bank, V vouched to invoice, ? open item) applied per cell, rendered as superscript ink annotations; the marginalia column accumulates the corresponding notes in Newsreader italic with the examiner's initials and timestamp, building a live working paper on screen.

The Benford's Law exhibit: a leading-digit distribution chart drawn as 1px ink-outlined bars with fine 45° hatch fills, the expected Benford curve as a thin dotted brass line, deviating digits' bars hatched in oxblood — captioned like a report figure ('Fig. 4 — First-digit distribution, vendor payments FY2024, n = 8,412') with an italic marginal note: 'Digit 7 over-represented 3.1×; see Schedule 5.'

The flagging moment: when the analyst marks a transaction suspect, no toast, no bounce — a 2px oxblood rule draws down the row's left edge like a pen stroke, the row takes the pale wash, a superscript '†' appears beside the amount, and simultaneously an entry sets itself into the Findings marginalia ('† $48,200 wire to Coral Gables entity — no supporting invoice'), while the running 'Amount in Question' counter in the masthead ticks upward digit-by-digit in mono. Quietly devastating, exactly like the profession.
